title: Universal Picard matching tested on a fixed-rank residue-field fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat proper locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Let $s\in S$ and $r\in\mathbb N$, with $q_s^*E$ finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Write $q_s:X_s\to X$ and $p_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ for the fibre projections [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field], and $E^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,\mathcal O_X)$. Then $R(f,E,\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-rank-match] holds iff either $X_s=\varnothing$, or both ordinary direct images $p_{s,*}q_s^*E$ and $p_{s,*}q_s^*(E^\vee)$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] are finite locally free of rank $r$. There is no assertion of topology or constructibility in this criterion.

proof.text: If X_s is empty, every further pullback is empty. Both ordinary direct images are zero and finite locally free of rank zero. The pullback of E on the empty scheme has rank zero, so the universal condition holds using the whole open.

Suppose X_s is nonempty. If the universal condition holds, test it on the identity of Spec kappa(s). The open neighbourhood of its unique point is the whole spectrum. Its chosen rank equals r, since E has rank r and the fibre has a point. Thus both ordinary direct images have rank r.

Conversely suppose those direct images have rank r. Perfect direct image and arbitrary base change for E and E dual identify them with degree-zero derived fibres. Over the field choose minimal finite-free models (Tag 0BCD): they have no negative terms, their degree-zero terms have rank r, and every differential is zero. In particular their outgoing degree-zero differentials are zero.

Pulling these models to any scheme over Spec kappa(s) keeps those differentials zero and computes ordinary direct images by derived base change. Their degree-zero cohomology is free of rank r, and pullback preserves the constant rank r of E. Restricting to the whole open gives the universal condition at every point. Composition of pullback squares identifies these modules with the ones in the definition of PicardUniversalRankMatch.

theorem picardUniversalRankMatch_residue_iff {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (r : ℕ) (s : S)
    (hEr : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))).obj E) r) :
    PicardUniversalRankMatch f E (S.fromSpecResidueField s) ↔
      IsEmpty (pullback f (S.fromSpecResidueField s) : Scheme.{u}) ∨
        (SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
          ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))).obj
            ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))).obj E)) r ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
          ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))).obj
            ((Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s))).obj
              (Modules.dual E))) r)
